kind: Cube workspace design references, not runtime captures
request: Rotatable cubes in 3D, visible face connection points, clicking a cube reveals its multiple modules together; at least five images.
scopeNotes: Cube containers and interaction controls are design proposals. No Unity runtime change or headset verification in this task.
Images 01, 02 and 05 illustrate spatial grouping and interaction. Their cable layouts are not an exact source dependency graph.
Image 03 contains all five CartState member modules simultaneously. White dotted lines are containment illustrations, not call edges.
Image 04 depicts ApplyCoupon calling CalculateTotal and IsValid, confirmed in CheckoutController.cs.
Image 06 foreground depicts CalculateTotal referencing DiscountPercent and the exact return expression. Background cable is illustrative, not a source call.
Rotation rings are interaction illustrations, not an axis or kinematics specification.

images.title: 큐브 기반 전체 3차원 공간
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE high-quality landscape 16:9 product design reference for DEPTH AI. Scene "01 / Cube workspace". This is a new design: a genuinely 3D cube-based source-code workspace, not the previous flat card design.

Scene: quiet cool silver-white spatial studio with a subtly gridded floor receding into depth, soft daylight, gentle background blur. No luxury skyline needed, no decorative props or people. Blue faceted hollow-cube brand emblem and DEPTH AI small at upper left. Pearl-white ceramic and clear optical glass with restrained blue and violet accents. Footer "Design reference / Not implemented".

CRITICAL GEOMETRY: all source/group objects are TRUE CUBES, equal width, height and depth, with six SQUARE faces and very lightly chamfered edges. NOT tablets, thin cards, rectangular slabs, elongated boxes, spheres, cylinders or hexagons. Show clear top and side faces; a cube should look like a graspable 3D box. The workspace occupies real volume at different X,Y,Z positions, not a grid on a screen plane.

Seven source-container cubes float at varied heights and distances around a small central source-linked project preview. Dominant near-center-right cube: "CartState" / "5 modules", its front face square, right and top faces fully visible. Other cubes, all genuine equal-sided cubes: "CheckoutController" / "4 modules", "CouponRules" / "2 modules", "CouponValidator" / "1 module", "TotalsView" / "1 module", "CartSummary" / "1 module", "Assets" / "2 images". Keep all labels legible, use small functional icons and empty space within faces, no code paragraphs. Each cube represents a container of source modules, NOT one entire application. A few faint smaller cubic silhouettes inside CartState communicate contents, without opening it yet.

Attach visible round CONNECTION PORTS to actual cube faces: blue sockets for function calls, violet for source references. Three thin softly curved cables join specific visible face ports across open 3D space; do not form a spiderweb and do not pass through faces or text. Ports remain mounted to the physical cube surface, not floating unrelated dots. Nearby CartState has a subtle thin blue selection outline and a small circular orbit affordance around its base.

A restrained small preview, off-center left and approximately 20% of image width, says "Checkout preview" and shows Ceramic mug $48, Indoor plant $72, Total $96. This preview can be a readable flat surface, but EVERY module object must be a true cube. A tiny world-space control strip says "Orbit space | Rotate cube | Open contents". Sparse X/Y/Z orientation gizmo in one corner. The composition must make it obvious the user can orbit this 3D environment, rotate each cube, see its connections, and open it to see several modules. Calm, polished, implementable, tangible volume. One image, not a collage.

Large CheckoutController cube at left-front, with front square face showing name and a concise internal port label "ApplyCoupon()". The cubes are at different XYZ positions; show their tops and sides clearly. This scene must make users understand exactly which two modules a selected connection joins, not an opaque web of random connections.
